programme: A circulating myeloid (monocyte/macrophage) differentiation, lipid-handling and matrix-remodeling module: EGR2 sets macrophage/microglial tissue identity, AEBP1 (via APOE, CD36, FABP4) drives lipid uptake and foam-cell-like polarization, FOSL1 (AP-1) couples this to MMP- and cytokine-driven tissue remodeling (MMP1/9/13, CCL2, IL6, CXCL8), while NR4A3 and HDAC7 govern the anti-inflammatory/resolution side of the same myeloid programme.
role_in_a: In COPD, this programme corresponds to smoking-activated monocytes differentiating into alveolar macrophages (EGR2-dependent tissue imprinting) that acquire a lipid-laden, MMP-secreting phenotype (AEBP1/FOSL1 targets) driving parenchymal matrix breakdown and emphysema, with NR4A3/HDAC7 acting on the resolution/anti-inflammatory arm.
role_in_b: In stroke, the same myeloid toolkit operates in two settings: circulating monocytes seeding atherosclerotic plaques as lipid-loaded macrophages (AEBP1/FOSL1 targets: CD36, FABP4, MMPs) whose instability precipitates the ischemic event, and resident microglia reusing EGR2- and NR4A3/HDAC7-linked transcriptional responses for post-ischemic neuroinflammation and repair (e.g. EGR2/BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy).
shared_axis: Both diseases are driven and monitored through the same circulating monocyte lineage, so a shared blood-derived transcriptional module for macrophage lipid handling and matrix remodeling is expected: in COPD it acts locally in the lung, in stroke it acts in the vessel wall (atherogenesis) and, after the event, in the brain via microglia descended from the same myeloid programme.
reasoning: The module is nameable from the factors' own target sets (lipid/foam-cell genes, AP-1/MMP remodeling, macrophage-identity and resolution factors) without needing outside knowledge, and EGR2 and NR4A3 are each independently placed in lung/macrophage and stroke/neuroinflammation contexts. But none of the retrieved papers state a COPD-stroke link directly, AEBP1 and FOSL1 carry no disease-specific literature at all, and HDAC7 evidence is stroke-only — so the cross-disease connection rests on the shared-monocyte-origin argument rather than on anything retrieved.
support: PMID 34797692 — EGR2 required for alveolar-macrophage tissue-specific imprinting (lung macrophage identity, COPD-relevant); PMID 42016821 — EGR2 governs microglial mitophagy (BNIP3L) after stroke; PMID 40571783 — exosomal EGR2 protects neurons via RNF8/DAPK1 in ischemia/reperfusion; PMID 36208355 — exosomal EGR2 ameliorates ischemic stroke via SIRT6; PMID 38474099 — NR4A3 (with NR4A2) modulates lung-cell responses relevant to COPD-adjacent physiology; PMID 40320842 — NR4A3 among targets for neuronal regeneration after ischemic stroke; PMID 38505917 — NR4A3 a hub gene in a rat middle-cerebral-artery-occlusion stroke model; PMID 34500302 — NR4A3 among transcription factors mediating neuroprotection in a stroke model; PMID 41229730 — HDAC7 knockout mitigates astrocyte reactivity/neuroinflammation post-stroke; PMID 40867143 — HDAC7 linked to neuroinflammation and epigenetic change in an aging ischemic-stroke model.
how_to_falsify: Profile monocytes/monocyte-derived macrophages from matched COPD and stroke (or high atherosclerotic-burden) cohorts and test whether EGR2, NR4A3, AEBP1, FOSL1 and HDAC7 co-vary with disease severity and with expression of their shared targets (CD36, FABP4, APOE, MMP1/9); if disease severity in one condition moves these factors and targets while the other shows no correlated shift, or ChIP/CUT&RUN in matched monocytes shows no shared binding at CD36/FABP4/MMP9 between the two patient groups, the shared circulating-myeloid mechanism is not supported.
caveats: Both networks are built from blood (circulating leukocyte/monocyte) profiling rather than lung or brain tissue directly, so the account describes a circulating myeloid signature, not confirmed resident alveolar-macrophage or microglial activity in situ. Support draws on 32-33 of 39 patient-group comparisons across 4 independent cohort pairs for the core factors, which is reasonably replicated, but the tissue-generic exclusion list removed the canonical immune/myeloid anchors (STAT1, CEBPB, IRF8, EZH2, KLF6, FOXO1, E2F1/2, ERG, NR3C2, SMAD3, TCF4) that would ordinarily anchor an inflammation story, meaning this account is necessarily built on the narrower, less-canonical residue. None of the single-view factors (TCF4, NPAS2, CIITA, NKX2-1, ZHX3, ARID1B) were used, consistent with their cohort-specific status.
